All tenses & aspects (controlled product.text: Produce the full English tense-aspect grid accurately, including perfect continuous and future perfect, choosing each for precise effect.
All tenses & aspects (controlled product.ex: 'By then I will have been working here for a decade.'

All tenses & aspects (controlled product.label: Recognise rare/literary forms
All tenses & aspects (controlled product.text: Read texts with marked forms ('be to', historic present, narrative inversion) and gloss their effect.

All tenses & aspects (controlled product.label: Production
All tenses & aspects (controlled product.text: Write a passage that deliberately deploys a wide, precise range of tenses.

Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.label: Conditional without 'if'
Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.text: Invert to drop 'if' in formal/literary style: 'Had I known... / Were she to refuse... / Should you need help...'.
Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.ex: 'Had they arrived earlier, all would have been well.'

Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.label: Map to standard conditionals
Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.text: Rewrite each inverted form as the equivalent if-clause and back. Register awareness.

Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.label: Production
Rare/literary structures (inversion in c.text: Use inverted conditionals appropriately in formal writing.

Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.label: Manage the timeline
Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.text: Coordinate past simple, past perfect and reported forms across a long narrative; use the historic present for vividness.
Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.ex: 'He had been waiting for hours when, suddenly, the door opens.'

Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.label: Optional backshift
Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.text: Note when backshift is optional (still-true facts: 'She said the Earth is/was round') and how it signals stance. Analysis.

Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.label: Production
Tense shifts in narrative & backshift su.text: Write/edit a narrative with controlled, purposeful tense shifts.

Aspectual nuance (stative vs dynamic, ha.label: Coerced statives
Aspectual nuance (stative vs dynamic, ha.text: Explore stative verbs used dynamically for effect ('I'm loving this', 'You're being silly') and the meaning shift this creates.

Aspectual nuance (stative vs dynamic, ha.label: Habitual & iterative shades
Aspectual nuance (stative vs dynamic, ha.text: Contrast 'used to / would / kept -ing / will (habitual)' for nuance. Fine-grained sorting.

Aspectual nuance (stative vs dynamic, ha.label: Production
Aspectual nuance (stative vs dynamic, ha.text: Exploit aspectual coercion deliberately in a stylistic text.

Adjective compounds & hyphenation.label: Form compound adjectives
Adjective compounds & hyphenation.text: Build hyphenated modifiers: 'a state-of-the-art system, a well-thought-out plan, a two-thirds majority.' Patterns: noun+participle, adverb+adjective, number+noun.

Adjective compounds & hyphenation.label: Hyphen rules
Adjective compounds & hyphenation.text: Hyphenate before the noun, usually not after; no hyphen after -ly adverbs ('a highly skilled worker'). Drill the conventions.

Adjective compounds & hyphenation.label: Production
Adjective compounds & hyphenation.text: Write descriptions using precise compound adjectives.

Adjectives in fixed expressions & idioms.label: Set collocations
Adjectives in fixed expressions & idioms.text: Master fixed adjective phrases: 'a foregone conclusion, a close call, common ground, a fine line, safe and sound.' Treat as wholes.

Adjectives in fixed expressions & idioms.label: Binomials
Adjectives in fixed expressions & idioms.text: Drill fixed-order pairs ('safe and sound', 'short and sweet', 'sick and tired') whose order can't be reversed.

Adjectives in fixed expressions & idioms.label: Production
Adjectives in fixed expressions & idioms.text: Weave fixed adjective expressions naturally into discourse.

Generic & impersonal 'one' / 'you' / 'th.label: Three impersonals
Generic & impersonal 'one' / 'you' / 'th.text: 'one' (formal generic: 'One should be careful'), 'you' (informal generic), 'they' (people/authorities unspecified: 'They say...'). Compare register.

Generic & impersonal 'one' / 'you' / 'th.label: Consistency
Generic & impersonal 'one' / 'you' / 'th.text: Keep the chosen pronoun consistent ('one... one's...', not switching to 'you'). Drill register-appropriate choice.

Generic & impersonal 'one' / 'you' / 'th.label: Production
Generic & impersonal 'one' / 'you' / 'th.text: Write the same general statement in three registers.

Logical & anticipatory 'it'.label: Postpone heavy subjects/objects
Logical & anticipatory 'it'.text: 'It' anticipates a clause: 'It is clear that... / I find it hard to believe that... / It was here that it happened.'
Logical & anticipatory 'it'.ex: 'It strikes me as odd that he agreed.'

Logical & anticipatory 'it'.label: Object 'it'
Logical & anticipatory 'it'.text: Anticipatory object: 'I owe it to you to explain / She made it clear that...'. Transformation drill.

Stylistic inversion & rhetorical syntax.label: Marked word order for effect
Stylistic inversion & rhetorical syntax.text: Deploy rhetorical inversion and balanced/periodic sentences: 'So intense was the heat that... / Not until later did we realise...'.

Stylistic inversion & rhetorical syntax.label: Parallelism & antithesis
Stylistic inversion & rhetorical syntax.text: Build parallel and antithetical structures for rhetorical force ('Not that I loved Caesar less, but that I loved Rome more').

Stylistic inversion & rhetorical syntax.label: Production
Stylistic inversion & rhetorical syntax.text: Craft a persuasive passage using inversion and balanced syntax.

Pragmatics: irony, implicature, understa.label: Meaning beyond words
Pragmatics: irony, implicature, understa.text: Decode and produce irony, conversational implicature (Grice) and British understatement ('not bad' = very good).

Pragmatics: irony, implicature, understa.label: Implied, not stated
Pragmatics: irony, implicature, understa.text: Analyse what is implicated rather than asserted ('Some passed' implies not all). Inference practice.

Pragmatics: irony, implicature, understa.label: Production
Pragmatics: irony, implicature, understa.text: Convey criticism or praise indirectly through understatement and irony.

Grammatical metalanguage.label: Vocabulary to analyse language
Grammatical metalanguage.text: Master terms to describe and correct English: clause, complement, modifier, aspect, transitivity, subordination, anaphora. Apply to sample sentences.
Grammatical metalanguage.ex: 'identify the subordinate clause and its function'

Grammatical metalanguage.label: Analyse & self-correct
Grammatical metalanguage.text: Parse complex sentences and explain errors using precise terminology. Peer-correction tasks.

Grammatical metalanguage.label: Production
Grammatical metalanguage.text: Annotate a text, labelling structures and justifying corrections.

Register & variation (BrE/AmE, formal/in.label: Systematic differences
Register & variation (BrE/AmE, formal/in.text: Compare BrE/AmE grammar (have got vs have, present perfect use, collective agreement, 'at the weekend' vs 'on the weekend') and formal/informal choices.

Register & variation (BrE/AmE, formal/in.label: Choose for context
Register & variation (BrE/AmE, formal/in.text: Select the variety/register a task or client expects. Sorting and rewriting across registers.

Register & variation (BrE/AmE, formal/in.label: Production
Register & variation (BrE/AmE, formal/in.text: Write one message in two varieties/registers for different audiences.

Disambiguating complex sentences.label: Spot the ambiguity
Disambiguating complex sentences.text: Locate scope, attachment and reference ambiguities: 'He told her he loved her at the party' (where?), negation scope, dangling modifiers.

Disambiguating complex sentences.label: Rewrite for one reading
Disambiguating complex sentences.text: Reorder, repunctuate, add a pronoun or split the sentence to fix a single meaning without losing nuance. Editing drill.

Disambiguating complex sentences.label: Production
Disambiguating complex sentences.text: Revise an ambiguous text so each sentence has one clear reading.

Formal written rhetoric & cohesion.label: Structure an argument
Formal written rhetoric & cohesion.text: Plan and signpost extended argument: thesis, development, counter-argument, synthesis, with cohesive ties across paragraphs.

Formal written rhetoric & cohesion.label: Cohesion & flow
Formal written rhetoric & cohesion.text: Manage theme/rheme progression, reference chains and transitions for seamless flow. Analyse a model essay.

Formal written rhetoric & cohesion.label: Production
Formal written rhetoric & cohesion.text: Write a cohesive argumentative essay with controlled rhetorical structure.
